b: Levon Aronian became the sole leader of the London Chess Classic Masters after scoring a second consecutive victory on Friday. Having defeated Shreyas Royal with black in round two, Aronian got the better of English legend Michael Adams with white in round three. The only other decisive result of the day saw 17-year-old Ukrainian rising star Ihor Samunenkov beating Royal - the reigning British champion is having a difficult time in London, having lost all three of his games so far.

Former co-leader Gawain Maroroa Jones signed a quick, seven-move draw with second seed Nihal Sarin and now shares second place with Andy Woodward and Nodirbek Abdusattorov. Both Woodward and Abdusattorov had the white pieces on Friday, though their games featured considerably more fighting chess. The three chasers stand on 2/3, half a point behind Aronian.

Saturday's fourth round will see Aronian taking on another of the most experienced players in the field, as he will have the black pieces against Vasyl Ivanchuk. Meanwhile, an encounter between two of the three players sharing second place will see Maroroa Jones playing white against Abdusattorov.

Challengers: Yip escapes with a draw, leads

Carissa Yip remains the sole leader of the Challengers after three rounds, though the American had to work hard to preserve her unbeaten record on Friday. Playing with black against Daniel Fernandez, the four-time US women's champion managed to escape with a draw from a difficult position. Yip thus goes into the fourth round with 2½/3.

Two games ended decisively in the third round: 12-year-old English prodigy Supratit Banerjee scored his second consecutive victory, inflicting a third defeat in as many games on Kazakh grandmaster Rinat Jumabayev, while 20-year-old Israeli grandmaster Eytan Rozen bounced back from his second-round loss by defeating experienced Polish GM Mateusz Bartel with the white pieces.
